observations: Photo 0, photo 1 and photo 2: a long rear-wheel-drive style automatic gearbox with a tail housing, still bolted to a V8 petrol engine, lying on the ground in a parts yard.
Photo 0 and photo 1: the engine is a V-type with two cylinder banks and a full wiring loom and hoses still attached.
Photo 0, photo 1 and photo 2: the gearbox case is covered in dirt, dry leaves and debris; the output shaft splines at the tail are exposed.
Photo 2: wiring connectors and hoses on top of the gearbox, no transmission tag or part number legible.
No brand logo, model tag or part number is readable on the gearbox or engine in any photo.
Background shows many other used engines and gearboxes; a 'GEARUP INC.' watermark and 'posted on Jiji' mark are on every photo.
Nothing in the photos shows the vehicle the unit came from, so the Ford Econoline fit rests on the seller's words.

identity.kind: used automatic gearbox for a V8 rear-wheel-drive van (seller says Ford Econoline E150 to E350)
read_from: photo 0 gearbox bolted to V8 engine

claims.claim: Gearbox for Ford Econoline E150 E250 E350 V8
claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show an automatic gearbox on a V8, consistent with the claim, but no Ford tag, part number or vehicle is shown.
Photos 0 to 2 show a used unit pulled with its engine in a parts yard, consistent with an imported used part.
Photos 0 to 2 show the case caked in dirt, leaves and debris, typical of a used yard part.
Pan gasket and case bolts are not shown close up, and even then opening cannot be ruled out remotely.
No clip of the unit running or shifting in a vehicle; it sits on the ground.
No receipt or warranty shown; an original receipt is unlikely for an imported yard part.

risks.risk: Gearbox is not the Econoline V8 unit claimed and will not fit the buyer's van.
risks.proof: Clear close photo of the transmission identification tag or casting part number on the case.
risks.if_unproven: as a gearbox of unconfirmed fit, lowest value in the class

risks.risk: Internal wear: slipping, burnt clutches, failed solenoids or torque converter.
risks.proof: Clip of the gearbox running and shifting through all gears in a vehicle, or a photo of the drained fluid and pan magnet.

risks.risk: Cracked case, broken mounting ears or damaged electrical connector hidden under the dirt.
risks.proof: Photos of the cleaned case from both sides and underneath, including the connector.

risks.risk: Torque converter, wiring harness or control module not included with the gearbox.
risks.proof: Photo of the gearbox alone, separated from the engine, with everything that comes with it.
risks.if_unproven: as bare gearbox without converter or harness

proof_requests: Close photo of the transmission tag or casting part number.
Clip of the gearbox shifting through all gears while running.
Photo of the gearbox separated from the engine showing what is included.
Photos of the case cleaned, both sides and underneath.
response.reason: The photos clearly show a used automatic gearbox for a V8 rear-wheel-drive vehicle, so it can be priced at its worst case as an untested core; 'like new' is contradicted by the dirty case, and the fit, tag and a running clip would raise it.
